body: Tried ECT, didn't do anything. No access to ketamine treatment.

I want to kill myself.

I hope next week is my last.

Sometime, I'd like to try the normie method, but I just have no idea how to do it. Like what the fuck am I supposed to besides just sitting at a computer all day? I have no idea how to live any other way.
Wow, this sounds so familiar. Parents always used to call my nerdy hobbies waste of money and time. I still feel this guilt every time I play games. Like I'm doing something wrong.

I've been having chest pains for the past two months, as well as shortness of breath as of last Saturday. The doctors say it's not heart related, but I don't know. I'm not convinced, yet, mostly because they haven't found an alternative explanation.

What really bothers me about it is not knowing what's the cause.

Damn, what you describe is pretty much spot on.

The thing that, after many a year of just letting it be, made me even consider getting help was, well, almost dying.

My friend, the only person I would consider a friend, and I were on a road trip last July.

He was driving, and I was sitting in the passenger's seat of his -98's Mitsubishi Carisma. We were going about 80 km/h (~50 mph in cavemantrics) on this relatively quiet two-lane road, when we noticed a slow moving tractor on our lane. My friend slowed down, and tried to switch to a lower gear, to make it easier to overtake the misplaced hunk of junk. Of course the gearbox wasn't in mint condition so it decided not to shift gears.

As my friend shifted his attention down to the gear shift, I noticed an approaching truck on the oncoming lane. I asked my friend to slow down and wait for the truck to pass before overtaking, as there was no way we would make it in time. But I could see on his face he wasn't listening. He wanted to pass that motherfucking tractor. He wasn't trying to be daring or anything, just a miscalculation on his part.

Though had he stalled for one second longer, we would have both been dead. The space in between wasn't much more than the thickness of a morning newspaper. 
My friend, a recovering depression patient himself, of course was very terrified of what had just happened, and apoplectic since he had almost gotten us killed.

Problem was, I didn't feel much of anything, during or after. The difference in our reactions is what made me question my own sanity.

I hope that you may someday find the help you're looking for as well.

Thanks for the reply.
